plan_for_our_own_game_server.phase_1_echo: UDP listener on a free port (e.g. 28970): answer getchallenge with challengeResponse, connect with connectResponse (mapname/gametype/sv_maxclients/protocol/shortversion), stats with statsResponse, using the 2697 XOR cipher
plan_for_our_own_game_server.phase_2_netchan: accept seq/serverId/messageAck headers exactly as SV_PacketEvent does, decode the bit-packed command stream (clc_move/clc_nop), and reply with a minimal gamestate + snapshot so the client leaves the loading screen
plan_for_our_own_game_server.phase_3_observe: because we own the server, log every received byte, the computed key, and the decoded command; expose a small HTTP or console query to dump client state
plan_for_our_own_game_server.phase_4_playable: add map/collision-free baseline gamestate and a snapshot loop so the client can stand and move; then bots and match end

caveats: do not copy 3.3.3.3 transport constants into the 1.1.1.13 path; the docs themselves warn they differ
the Python zip is a lobby/auth server, not a game server; it does not provide in-game gamestate/snapshot logic
the toolchain for building the Rust/C server is still missing locally (choco mingw failed); a Python server avoids that dependency and can be built immediately
recommendation: write the game server in Python first (reuses our working cipher code and needs no toolchain), inside tools/ or a new server1649370/ package, with exhaustive logging from day one.
